topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final course lecture and outlines the core learning outcomes regarding cancer therapy approaches and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain conventional cancer treatments aimed at physically removing or non-specifically destroying dividing cells, detailing their administration, toxicities, and drug resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how intrinsic cellular defects and physiological dependencies unique to cancer cells can be selectively targeted to induce growth arrest or apoptosis.

topics.label: Oncogene Addiction and Kinase Inhibitor Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the identification of driver oncogenes, the application of small-molecule kinase inhibitors to exploit oncogene addiction, and the diverse mechanisms by which tumors acquire drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Therapeutics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered antibodies targeting tumor-cell surface antigens are used to block oncogenic signaling, induce immune-mediated cytotoxicity, or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Tumor Immune Surveillance and Checkpoint Inhibition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence for immune surveillance against tumors and explain how immune checkpoint inhibitors reactivate endogenous T cells to target cancer neoantigens.

topics.label: Engineered T-Cell Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss engineered immunotherapies that artificially bridge or genetically reprogram T cells to destroy cancer cells, highlighting their mechanisms, clinical efficacy, and current limitations.

topics.label: Overarching Challenges, Outcomes, and Future Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide a broad appraisal of cancer therapy by addressing population-level survival trends, treatment barriers such as heterogeneity, and emerging future priorities in clinical practice.
